body.statement:
Let \(K\) be an effective ordered field and let a semialgebraic subset of a real closed extension of \(K\) be described by a Boolean formula in \(n\) variables involving at most \(s\) polynomial sign conditions of degree at most \(d\). Exact bounded-algebraic-sampling and existential-realizability algorithms decide whether the set is empty and, when it is nonempty, return a real-univariate representation of a sample point with Thom sign data. The same assertion holds after adjoining one further polynomial sign condition and over a finite real algebraic extension of \(K\), with algebraic degree measured relative to that coefficient field. Real-univariate representation, multiplication-matrix, square-free-factorization, Thom-sign, and root-isolation algorithms normalize a finite real-algebraic tower to a square-free univariate representation over the original field without increasing the field degree. There are explicit coordinatewise nondecreasing bounds \(\mathsf{Samp}\) and \(\mathsf{Exist}\) for the numbers of generated algebraic records and their relative algebraic degrees, and corresponding integer-coefficient height bounds, including the final tower-normalization and root-isolation height. For a universal constant \(c\geq 1\), the record-count and relative-degree bounds may be chosen no larger than
\[
 (s+d+2)^{c(n+1)^c},
\]
and, when the integer input coefficients have binary length at most \(h\), the output coefficient and isolating-endpoint lengths may be chosen no larger than
\[
 (h+1)^{(s+d+2)^{c(n+1)^c}}.
\]

source.locator: Algorithms 13.1 and 14.5 and their complexity analyses in Chapters 13--14; real-univariate representations, Thom encodings, multiplication matrices, and integer bit complexity in Chapters 10--14

attestation.note: The stable Springer source and the algorithm locations were checked; the displayed bound is a conservative singly exponential envelope of the cited bounded-algebraic-sampling and existential-realizability bounds.
